front.title: Defining a Celestial Bodies Reference Framework for Deep Space Internet Addressing

abstract.t: This document highlights the operational framework within Deepspace/ TIPTOP protocols to utilize an external, standardized reference framework for celestial objects, functioning as an equivalent to ISO 3166 for interplanetary networking. To avoid operational overhead and duplication of effort, this framework defers the definitions, naming, and tracking of celestial entities directly to the International Astronomical Union (IAU) and the Minor Planet Center (MPC). This document outlines how these external identifiers guide hierarchical address allocation without requiring IANA to maintain a dedicated astronomical nomenclature registry. The ultimate objective is to establish a clear definition of what constitutes a valid Celestial Body for networking purposes. From a resource-management perspective, this framework remains identical regardless of whether the target location hosts human colonies, scientific equipment, or autonomous robotic assets; any entity requiring internet and communication access must rely on a stable celestial anchor.
